data.name: Rajani
data.gender_notes: Rajani is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Ratn' (Jewel) and 'Rani' (Queen), Rajani means 'Queen of the night' or 'Night of jewels'. It is an exquisite and majestic name, evoking images of the moon and its queen, Chandra. The name Rajani carries the meaning “Queen's night” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Rajani usually hope their child will grow to embody queen's night and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the radiance and grace of the divine feminine.
data.etymology: Rajani belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Queen's night.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rajani total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: Rajani is an elegant and captivating name in Hindu culture. It is believed to bring grace, beauty, and a sense of elegance to one's persona. The name is often associated with the night, the moon, and the divine feminine, instilling a sense of mystery and allure.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Rajani is often associated with the divine feminine energy or Shakti. It represents the nurturing, creative, and protective aspects of the divine, embodying the essence of the goddesses Lakshmi (Goddess of wealth and prosperity), Parvati (Consort of Shiva), and Saraswati (Goddess of knowledge and wisdom). Rajani serves as a reminder to honor the inner queen or goddess within us and to seek her guidance and grace in all aspects of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rajani symbolizes the grace and elegance of the moon in the night sky. Her name derives from 'Raja' (king) and 'Ani' (night), reflecting her role as the celestial queen illuminating the darkness with her gentle, calming light.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Rajani is mentioned in the Mahabharata as the name of a princess of the Vidarbha kingdom. The name Rajani carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
